verdict: Yum! sold Pizza Hut during the quarter for a $1.7B pre-tax gain that swamped everything else — GAAP profit hit $1.6B — while the brands it kept grew revenue 4%, led by KFC.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $1.41 a year ago, lifted by the Pizza Hut sale gain

kpis.label: EPS excl. Special Items
kpis.note: Yum!'s underlying per-share profit, without the sale gain

segments.name: KFC
segments.note: Fried-chicken restaurants worldwide — company-owned sales plus franchise royalties and advertising contributions. System sales were $10.0B, up 8%.

segments.name: Taco Bell
segments.note: Mexican-inspired fast food. Revenue rose 5% even though U.S. same-store sales fell 4% in the quarter.

segments.name: Pizza Hut
segments.note: Pizza Hut's revenue through its sale dates only — mainland China was sold on August 7, 2026 and the rest on September 1, 2026 — so this line will not recur.

segments.name: Habit Burger & Grill
segments.note: Chargrilled burgers, all in the U.S. — 390 restaurants, about four-fifths company-owned. Revenue was flat year over year.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Head-office and brand support costs — running the company behind the restaurants.

opex.name: Franchise advertising and other services
opex.note: Spending the advertising funds collected from franchisees — it roughly matches the contributions collected in revenue.

opex.name: Franchise and property expenses
opex.note: Costs of properties Yum! owns and leases on to franchisees.

opex.name: Refranchising gain
opex.note: A gain, not a cost: Yum! sold company-owned restaurants to franchisees for more than their book value.

opex.name: Other income
opex.note: Small miscellaneous income items, net — this line reduces total costs.

otherDetail: A $1,683M pre-tax gain on the Pizza Hut divestitures, less $120M of net interest expense and $2M of other pension expense (and $1M of rounding in the printed millions) — net $1,560M. Yum!'s printed operating profit including the gain was $2,317M.
oneTimers: Pre-tax gain of $1,683M on selling Pizza Hut — mainland China to Yum China (August 7, 2026) and the rest of the world to LongRange Capital (September 1, 2026). It is why GAAP EPS was $5.92 versus $1.56 excluding Special Items.
Pizza Hut contributed $202M of revenue and $50M of operating profit through its sale dates; neither will recur, and year-ago comparisons included a full quarter of Pizza Hut.
Refranchising gain of $22M from selling company restaurants to franchisees.

takeaways.title: The Pizza Hut sale is the quarter
takeaways.text: Selling Pizza Hut booked a $1,683M pre-tax gain and took GAAP net income to $1,623M. Excluding Special Items, EPS was $1.56, and core operating profit excluding Pizza Hut grew 1%.

takeaways.title: KFC carried the growth
takeaways.text: KFC revenue rose 8% to $948M on $10.0B of system sales, with 878 gross new restaurants and unit growth of 7%. KFC is now well over half of Yum!'s ongoing business.

takeaways.title: Taco Bell U.S. had a soft quarter
takeaways.text: Taco Bell U.S. same-store sales fell 4% and division operating profit fell 5% to $255M, though Yum! says Taco Bell U.S. has outpaced the fast-food industry on same-store sales since the end of September.

footerNote: Yum! prints the $1,683M Pizza Hut divestiture gain between total costs and operating profit. This chart shows operating profit before that one-time gain ($635M) and puts the gain in Other income below, so the underlying restaurant business stays readable; printed operating profit including the gain was $2,317M (the printed millions also carry a $1M rounding difference, absorbed in Other income). Division revenues are the total revenues printed for each division in the release and 10-Q.
